provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)
provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: The intervention was delivered by the same enumerators who conducted the baseline and endline surveys, which may bias endline self-reported economic activity because respondents may know and trust the team better; the evaluator finds this concerning for interpreting reports of economic activity.
issues.quote: the intervention was delivered by the same enumerators who conducted the baseline and endline surveys. This is a bit concerning because it introduces the possibility of endline reporting varying

issues.text: Enumerator involvement likely violates the exclusion restriction for the 2SLS strategy, which assumes treatment affects outcomes only through increased knowledge; the evaluator suggests the authors consider dropping 2SLS in favour of correlational analysis.
issues.quote: I also think it leads to an exclusion restriction violation for the 2SLS strategy, which currently assumes the treatment can only operate through the channel of improving knowledge.

issues.text: The accountability measure (whether the firm gives an opinion on whether taxes are put to good use, excluding 'I don't know') is indirect and hard to interpret as accountability, since 'I don't know' or a 'yes' may reflect many things other than demand for accountability.
issues.quote: the measure of accountability is, in my mind, quite indirect and a bit difficult to interpret as accountability.

issues.text: The emphasis on the fiscal contract and accountability framing may be unwarranted given the indirect accountability measure.
issues.quote: I wonder if it is wise to emphasize the fiscal contract and accountability as much here

issues.text: Table 10 (showing a negative treatment effect on a government performance question) is not referred to in the text, and it is unclear whether it measures accountability; the evaluator thinks it should be brought more closely into the analysis.
issues.quote: I did not see Table 10 referred to in the text.

issues.text: The reduction in tax payments on the extensive margin is not clearly interpreted: it is unclear whether smaller firms stopped paying non-TPU taxes after learning they are exempt from them, and the manuscript does not make this explicit.
issues.quote: I was not clear if we can interpret this reduction in payment as (smaller) firms realizing that they are exempt from other non-TPU taxes and stopping paying those?

issues.text: Treated firms were more likely to report that the hypothetical firm would have declared zero revenue, suggesting smaller firms learned they can self-declare zero, an alternative explanation for negative payment effects; the paper provides no table examining treatment effects on self-declaring zero.
issues.quote: Why is there not a table looking at the effect of treatment when self-declaring a zero?

issues.text: The receipt-based compliance measure is insufficiently described: it is unclear whether it covers only TPU receipts and how receipts were validated (photographs versus enumerator perceptions).
issues.quote: it would help to discuss (i) whether this only includes TPU receipts, (ii) how receipts were validated

issues.text: The increase in reported orders and revenues may reflect better book-keeping induced by the treatment (firms paying more attention to sales) rather than real economic activity; the evaluator asks the authors to test this with survey data.
issues.quote: firms simply pay more attention to their orders and revenue, i.e. by improving their book-keeping?

issues.text: The information content of the treatment is inadequately described; Figure 1 shows only a tax on advertising, which is not much discussed, and a fuller (translated) summary of the intervention content is needed.
issues.quote: I found the information provided about the content of the taxpayer information intervention to be limited.

issues.text: The small sample size limits power, especially with heterogeneity analyses on sample splits; the evaluator asks for power calculations for these subgroup splits (Figures 7-8) as were provided for the main results.
issues.quote: It might be nice to do the same thing for the sample splits considered in the heterogeneity analysis (Figures 7-8).

issues.text: It is unclear whether tax collectors were aware of the intervention and could change audit targeting as Proposition 1 implies; the variation in firm size in the sample is small, making such responses hard to observe.
issues.quote: whether tax collectors were sufficiently aware of the intervention to change their audit targeting strategies?

issues.text: The authors state the treatment could affect the likelihood of a tax visit but do not test this directly; the evaluator asks why they do not test it.
issues.quote: Can't they test whether the treatment affected the likelihood of a visit directly?
